title: Understanding Principal Components
text: Principal components are the directions in which the data varies the most. In PCA, we aim to capture as much variance as possible with the fewest components.

title: Explained Variance in PCA
text: The explained variance indicates how much information (variance) is captured by each principal component. As you add more components, the cumulative explained variance increases.

title: Interpreting the Scree Plot
text: A scree plot shows the explained variance for each principal component. Typically, the plot will show a sharp decline followed by a plateau. The point where the plot levels off is often used to determine the number of components to keep.

title: Evaluating the Statement
text: Based on the scree plot, determine if adding more components continues to significantly increase the explained variance.
